questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A very foreign place with good living conditions and high academic level

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Compared to my study abroad in Switzerland, everything was non-trivial. 
Not easy to navigate the information -- and you will need a lot of Papago/Google Translate, even for university pages.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Contacts are available for assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
No orientation was held for a majority of the exchange students. Some departments held their own welcomes -- but weeks into the semester.
I suspect this might be covid-related, but do not expect a lot of assistance if you do not ask for it.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I booked an AirBNB for a week's duration (a little tight) -- in this week I went to local housing agencies which showed lots of available affordable properties close to the campus. The agencies are also commonly used for local students who do not get into the dormitory. Alternatively check
m.place.naver.com
. This is much preferred to the goshiwons. Very easy to find housing, however be careful about scams on social media. Be observant about your room's condition, e.g. presence of mold etc. -- they often do not care about these things as much as we do.
It's difficult to get these rentals for 1-2 months but very easy for, e.g., a duration of 4 months+.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Places near the university shuttle buses are also convenient -- check these. Often the real estate agents also know about this and can guide you. Be critical and check many places out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Don't expect to get into the campus dorm. PhD (not MSc) students may have a higher chance, but otherwise for this option, basically only the shared rooms are possible.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy, but generally an annoying course handbook. So many of the graduate courses are removed and added each year so consider contacting the dept. about courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Be aware of the registration opening time. Use
time.is
to be ready to register to your courses. You will likely have to compete with the local students while you still are in Denmark. If you miss a course, contact the prof -- it's very often possible to get in the course anyway (if you make contact right away)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much, but a lot of pdfs are provided.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: None of the classes I originally wanted were held this year (they were held the previous year), but I succesfully registered for the four new courses I wanted. Note that many people often miss the registration on popular courses since relatively few spots are available.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be quick, sign up for more courses than you want and drop them later (although they cannot have any time overlap), consider the order in which you register for them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good selection of English courses (graduate level) compared to many other Asian universities.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Very varying difficulty since they group together MSc and PhD level courses. 
They are however very transparent about the difficulties, and the first week is for making sure you're aware of the contents.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar, but much less feedback and interaction with TAs. Exams are almost exclusively written. They have midterms and often grade based on many things, e.g. how often you meet up. Only one of my teachers kept track of this, however, so don't be too scared.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Natural Language Processing
Financial Development of the World
Geometric Methods for High-Dimensional Data Analysis 
Korean Language Class

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend taking a unique course like Geometric Methods to build your academic profile. I further recommend taking either the language class SNU offers or the one at their language institute.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing concretely comes to mind, perhaps because there were too many

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Many deposits are quite high, e.g. between 5 and 15 times monthly rent for apt.
Also, 330 000 krw deposit for credit card (Woori)

Fruit and yoghurt is relatively expensive

Eating out is really cheap, so do that a lot!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Crazy amount of things

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: SNU buddy -- and go with these people for various random things

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: dates

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: As long as you get your basic worries in place quickly for the whole period (bank, sim, accommodation, figuring out how to get around, practical registration + immigration things), you will be able to adjust more stress-free. It wasn't too difficult for me to get used to the culture -- try to act a bit like they do

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Ask them anything, they are so helpful

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Biking difficulties.
Non-students are pretty bad at English, so use translation apps a lot.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Korean friendliness to foreigners -- just say gamsahamnida (thank you) and they will be so happy.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Use Korean greetings. Always! be respectful :) 
Take part in the SNU buddy events
Try lots of crazy food (sannakji!)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Open a bank account at Woori or Shinhan before the semester starts 
Use Coupang (or gmarket) for cheap everything
Buy the Chingu mobile pre-paid plan
You will likely receive your ARC very late
Make use of the short semester to travel a bit around before you have to go back :) Japan and especially Taiwan were super nice.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing another world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Doing well academically with so many available distractions

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I already miss Korea

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
